Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation today — great to hear more about the Acme Analytics pilot scope and timeline. Quick recap and a couple of procurement questions so we can keep momentum:

- Scope: 10 dedicated seats for 3 months, endpoint for embeddings + chat, expected peak qps ~20.
- Pilot objectives: measure cost-per-inference, latency at 2k token seq, and integration work for the feature flag rollout.

Procurement / commercial path questions (need to confirm before we send paperwork):
1) Preferred payment method: do you plan to pay via PO (Net30) or corporate card? If PO, who is the procurement contact and billing address?
2) Vendor setup: does Acme require a vendor intake packet (W-9/W-8, banking details)? If so, what fields are required and how should we submit (vendor portal email or upload)?
3) Marketplace: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace (SaaS subscription) or direct contract? Marketplace can simplify approvals but has different billing terms.

If you can confirm 1-3, I’ll loop in our finance/ops team and send over the W-9/vendor packet and the standard order form/DocuSign link.

Next steps: 
- You confirm procurement path (PO vs card) and expected PO date
- I’ll send W-9 and vendor_setup_packet and DocuSign order form

Thanks — excited to get this started.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our internal notes. Procurement will handle vendor setup. A few items from procurement:

- We prefer PO / Net30 for pilots (finance policy). We'll need a completed vendor setup packet and a W-9 on file to create a vendor record.
- Banking details (ACH) can be submitted via our secure vendor portal once the vendor record is created — can you confirm the format they require (routing + acct or wire instructions)?
- We prefer marketplace purchases when possible, but legal requires confirmation that the SaaS terms match our enterprise requirements. Do you have an AWS Marketplace listing or a marketplace-managed contract option?

I’ve attached our intake form (procurement_intake_acme.pdf) for reference — it asks for contact person, tax ID, W-9, remit address, and invoice preferences.

Tentative timeline: If we have the vendor packet and W-9 this week, procurement can provision the vendor record next week and issue a PO by 03/02. 

Thanks,

Marissa —

Confirmations below:

1) PO / Net30: Yes, we can accept PO with Net30 terms for pilots. We require a signed order form referencing our standard MSA. Sales ops can countersign. No minimums for pilot deals but we require the signed order form or DocuSign.

2) W-9 & vendor packet: Attached are the Redwood_W9_2026.pdf and redwood_vendor_setup_packet_acme.docx. The vendor packet contains Tax ID, remittance address, and optional ACH instructions. Banking (ACH) details should not be emailed in the clear; advise Acme to upload into their vendor portal or we can provide a secure upload link (https://payments.redwood.com/secure-upload). We can also accept wire instructions if required.

3) Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (SaaS subscription). If Acme wants to transact via Marketplace, they can purchase directly there; note marketplace transactions route billing through AWS and may have different contract terms and delay on invoicing. If you prefer direct PO invoicing to Redwood, use the signed order form route.

4) DocuSign / order form: Standard MSA + order form is available here: https://docusign.com/standard_msa_redwood. Sales ops (rishi_malhotra) is the contact for countersign.

Next steps (recommended): I’ll hand these attachments to you — once you send them to Samantha, ask for the expected PO date and whether procurement will use marketplace or direct PO.

-Dev
